attempts.summary: Configured policy-based egress on node3 (RHEL7) so TCP traffic to node4:8080 is steered across the first transit network (node1 eth1 10.10.1.0/30 ↔ node2 vtnet1) and TCP traffic to node4:9090 across the second transit network (node1 eth2 10.10.2.0/30 ↔ node2 vtnet2), with both flows successfully reaching node4 over the shared 10.100.106.0/24 network as the final hop. Implementation: iptables mangle marks + policy ip rules/routes on node3 (RHEL7, persisted via firewalld direct rules + NetworkManager dispatcher script), VyOS policy-route ruleset with two static routing tables on node1, and OPNsense opt1/opt2 interfaces + pf pass rules on node2. All four nodes were restarted one at a time (native reboot mechanisms), boot-identity change was proven for each (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD/OPNsense), and post-restart the full configuration, routing, firewall rules, and end-to-end port-8080/port-9090 flows over their respective distinct transit networks were reverified via tcpdump captures on node1's and node2's transit interfaces.
